blocks.text: New Year's Day is my favourite day to be at Bondi. While the rest of Sydney sleeps off the fireworks, the beach wakes up soft and golden, the water is clean and cool, and there's a quiet camaraderie among everyone who made it down for a swim. Here's how I'd spend it - an early dip, a slow breakfast, and a long lunch with the Pacific glittering below.

Here's what first-timers get wrong: January 1 at Bondi isn't a party on the sand. Bondi Beach is a permanent alcohol-free and glass-free zone that Waverley Council enforces, so the celebrating happens on the promenade and inside the venues, not on the beach. Once you know that, the day falls into place.

My New Year's Day ritual is a morning ocean swim - nothing washes off the old year like cold salt water. For laps, the Bondi Icebergs ocean pool at the south end is the classic choice; check their site for swim hours and fees, which vary, and the pool sometimes closes for swell. If you'd rather just float, the calmer water is usually down the north end near the flags. When you climb out, [The Crabbe Hole](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/the-crabbe-hole) - the tiny café tucked beneath the Icebergs pool - does the best post-swim coffee on this side of the beach, if you can beat the locals to a stool.

blocks.title: Swim between the flags
blocks.text: Bondi is patrolled by Surf Life Saving lifeguards, but rips are real and New Year's Day brings big, sometimes tired crowds into the water. Always swim between the red-and-yellow flags, and if the surf looks heavy, the Icebergs pool or the gentler north corner is the smarter call.
The long lunch - Bondi's real New Year tradition

The heart of New Year's Day here is a long lunch with a view. [Icebergs Dining Room and Bar](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/icebergs-dining-room-and-bar), over the south end since it opened in 2002, has long been the glamorous centre of Bondi's New Year and still puts on a special sitting for the day. Other clifftop and beachfront restaurants run festive lunches too - details change every year, so check each venue's own site for this year's plans.

And if Icebergs is booked out (it goes early), Bondi has plenty of other tables with the Pacific in view. [Sean's](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/seans) is the north end's quietly iconic long-lunch institution, [North Bondi Fish](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/north-bondi-fish) sits right above the sand where the promenade curves north, and [Bondi Trattoria](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/bondi-trattoria) has watched the beach from Campbell Parade for decades. For the full sweep of tables with an ocean view, browse our guide to [Bondi's beachfront and ocean-view dining](/bondi-eat-and-drink/waterfront-dining-bondi-beach) - then book whichever one calls to you, direct.

blocks.title: Book direct, and book early
blocks.text: New Year's Day menus, prices and session times at these venues change every year and sell out fast - often weeks ahead. I won't quote a price that might be stale; check each venue's website or booking page and reserve directly.

For the same southern view without the fine-dining price tag, [The Bergs Bistro](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/the-bergs-bistro-bondi-icebergs-club) - one flight up in the Bondi Icebergs Club, just below the famous Dining Room - is the local's-know option: honest food, the same clifftop outlook, and far easier on the New Year budget. Sign in at the door and book ahead, because it fills up too.

If a set menu isn't your speed, Bondi's cafés along Campbell Parade and Hall Street do a roaring recovery-brunch trade on January 1. [Lox Stock & Barrel](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/lox-stock-and-barrel) on Hall Street and [Speedos Cafe](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/speedos-cafe) up the north end are two of my go-tos for eggs and strong coffee, but there's no shortage of poached eggs a short walk from the sand - our full guide to [Bondi's best breakfast and brunch](/bondi-eat-and-drink/breakfast-brunch-bondi-beach) has the rest. Just expect a wait, and be kind to the staff.

Bring a hat, reef-safe sunscreen and your own water bottle. January is peak Sydney summer and the promenade offers almost no shade - I've watched too many visitors get fried by 11am. There are public bubblers to refill along the beach.
Getting there (leave the car at home)

Don't drive to Bondi on New Year's Day if you can avoid it. Parking is scarce and metered, and streets near the beach are often hit by New Year's road closures and clean-up. Public transport is easier: take a train to Bondi Junction, then a bus - the 333 and 380 both run to Bondi Beach. Check Transport for NSW for live timetables, as holiday services differ from a normal day.

blocks.title: Find your table
blocks.text: This is just my New Year's shortlist. Our [Bondi eat & drink directory](/bondi-eat-and-drink) lists every café, restaurant, bar and bakery on the beach - 160+ venues you can filter by cuisine, area, price or who you're with, so whether you're after a clifftop lunch, a recovery brunch or a quiet coffee, you can find the right table before you head down.

items.q: Can you drink alcohol on Bondi Beach on New Year's Day?
items.a: No. Bondi Beach is a permanent alcohol-free and glass-free zone enforced by Waverley Council, on New Year's Day too. The celebrating happens inside the venues and up on the promenade, not on the sand.

items.q: Is Icebergs open on New Year's Day?
items.a: Icebergs has long marked New Year's Day, these days as a relaxed sit-down lunch. Sittings, menus and prices change each year and book out early, so check its website and reserve directly. If the Dining Room is full, the more casual Bergs Bistro in the same building, or other ocean-view rooms like Sean's and North Bondi Fish, are worth a call.

items.q: What's the best time to go to Bondi on New Year's Day?
items.a: Early. A swim before roughly 10am means calmer water, easier café tables and a parking spot if you must drive. By midday the beach and cafés are packed.

items.q: How do I get to Bondi on New Year's Day?
items.a: Take public transport. Catch a train to Bondi Junction, then the 333 or 380 bus to the beach. Holiday timetables differ, so check Transport for NSW first and expect road closures near the beach.

items.q: Is it worth going to Bondi on New Year's Day?
items.a: Absolutely, if you go for the right reasons - a clean morning swim, a slow brunch and a long lunch with an ocean view. It's a calmer, more local celebration than New Year's Eve.

blocks.text: That's my New Year's Day: swim early, eat slowly, book ahead and let the beach set the pace. Leave the fireworks-night frenzy behind and you'll find the version of Bondi we locals quietly keep for ourselves. Happy new year - see you in the water.
